title: 1Password says an attacker used an employee's GitHub account to download account records of a subset of users; vaults not affected
date_note: Date of 1Password's own update; the post gives no earlier disclosure day. 1Password began investigating on 19 November.
geo_basis: Keitai Watch describes 1Password as developed and operated by a Canadian company; pin at country level
summary: 1Password says it began investigating on 19 November after signs an attacker had accessed an employee's corporate GitHub account. It says the attacker used it to reach source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded account records for a subset of users, including names and email addresses; source code was copied from private repositories and the CI/CD system accessed. 1Password says customer vaults were not affected.
plain: 1Password says an attacker got into an employee's GitHub account and took some customers' names, emails and account metadata. The company says password vaults were not touched.
exec: A password-manager vendor reports source code and some customer account records were taken; it says vault contents were not accessed.
action: 1Password advises you do not need to update anything in your account, to be cautious of unexpected emails, texts or calls mentioning 1Password, and never to give your account password or Secret Key to anyone.
impact: Account records of a subset of users; vault contents not affected, according to 1Password.

validation.note: 1Password's own post is the primary source; Keitai Watch (Impress) and ITmedia Enterprise relay it.

review.note: Merged duplicate 1password-backend-unauthorized-access (same post); added ITmedia source; summary adds malicious code push to backend; sectors/surface basis inferred; validation primary.
